subject: Activation credit schedule and slab discounting for NimblePay pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Brooks <samuel.brooks@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Activation credits and discount bands — proposal for pilot

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table for the 6‑week pilot and the follow-on commercial bands so your team can review with procurement. High level: we can pair a small activation credit pool with a clear usage-to-discount ramp so NimblePay has predictable economics as you scale.

Proposal (summary):
- Activation credits: $10,000 in platform credits to cover pilot sentiment testing and initial integrations (applies to token usage only).
- Pilot window: 6 weeks from sign — up to 1M tokens covered by activation credits, then standard list pricing if exceeded.
- Post-pilot conversion: three purchase bands (monthly equivalent committed spend):
  • Band A — $0–$25k/mo: 5% per-token discount + access to standard SLA
  • Band B — $25k–$75k/mo: 12% per-token discount + preferred routing / reduced cold-start latency allocation
  • Band C — $75k+/mo: 20% per-token discount + dedicated capacity evaluation (reserved ingress pools)
- Ramp & credits clause: If NimblePay converts to a committed band within 90 days after pilot, Redwood will apply any unused activation credits as a one‑time offset to the first billing cycle.

Operational notes / asks:
- Can you confirm the internal contact for procurement and the proposed PO cadence?
- Do you need a separate SOC2 evidence package for SSO/KMS? We can attach the standard pack.

Attachments: pricing comparison and term sheet attached for procurement review ([attachment: NimblePay-PRICING-COMPARISON.xlsx], [attachment: redwood-activation-term-sheet.pdf]).

If that all looks reasonable we can produce a short SOW + order form and aim to start the pilot next week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before I loop procurement: 

1) The $10k activation credit — does it cover embeddings and chat generation equally? We run a mix of both in the pilot.
2) If we exceed the 1M token cap inside the 6 weeks, will you throttle or bill on the spot? We prefer to keep the pilot experience uninterrupted.
3) About the unused credits being applied post-conversion: is that limited to list price offsets only, or can it be applied against committed discount amortization?

Also attaching our internal SOW outline for context — that's a separate doc but should help align expectations ([attachment: nimblepay-sow-draft.pdf]).

If you can confirm answers, I’ll get procurement to look at the XLS and term sheet.

—Sam

> 
> Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before I loop procurement: 
> 
> 1) The $10k activation credit — does it cover embeddings and chat generation equally? We run a mix of both in the pilot.
> 2) If we exceed the 1M token cap inside the 6 weeks, will you throttle or bill on the spot? We prefer to keep the pilot experience uninterrupted.
> 3) About the unused credits being applied post-conversion: is that limited to list price offsets only, or can it be applied against committed discount amortization?

Hi Sam — quick answers: 
- Coverage: Activation credits apply across token‑based units (generation + embeddings). We'll include a short usage mapping in the SOW so both sides have the same denominator.
- Overage behavior: For pilots we do not throttle; we'll allow soft overage with on‑demand billing at list price and notify you at 80% of the credit. If you want unlimited trial experience we can offer a temporary soft cap waiver but we typically prefer to track usage.
- Application of unused credits: Credits will be applied as a one‑time invoice credit at list price. They are not amortized against committed discounts (i.e., they offset the first invoice before discount applies). We can discuss alternate accounting treatment if your procurement team requires it, but it will change the commercial calculus.

Next steps: Jordan and I can produce an abbreviated SOW + order form with the 6‑week schedule and a usage mapping table. If NimblePay confirms procurement contact, we’ll push the docs to DocuSign.

Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Ben — that all helps. Procurement contact is Maria Lopez (maria.lopez@nimblepay.com). She’ll review the XLS and term sheet; I’ve copied procurement on this thread. Two small asks from them:

- Can the activation credit be split so $7k applies to generation and $3k to embeddings (they want visibility per cost bucket)?
- They asked whether the Band B (12% discount) can be time-bound (12 months once committed) rather than indefinite. That’s normally what they look for in supplier agreements.

If Redwood is fine with those two, Maria will circulate a PO and we can DocuSign the short SOW. We’re aiming to start integration the week of Nov 22.

—Sam
